books.section: Topic 3.12 Movement in the Early Republic

stimulus.text: Paraphrase: Between 1791 and 1810, more than 25,000 refugees reached the United States from Saint-Domingue, the French colony that became Haiti. They fled the slave revolt that began there in 1791 and the fighting that followed. In the spring and summer of 1793, about 2,000 refugees arrived in Philadelphia, and by 1794 more than 3,000 had reached the city. The refugees included white planters, free people of color, and enslaved people brought by their owners. Philadelphians raised nearly $14,000 to help the newcomers. Other refugees landed in Charleston and other Atlantic ports.
stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase drawn from the Smithsonian Magazine account of the Saint-Domingue refugee arrivals, 1791-1810, and the account of the 1793 Philadelphia yellow fever epidemic; figures checked against those sources.

source: original; stimulus paraphrased from the Smithsonian Magazine account of the Saint-Domingue refugee arrivals.
stem: The refugees included white planters, free people of color, and enslaved people. What does that mix show about the revolt?

options.text: Only enslaved people suffered from the fighting.
options.misconception: Planters and free people of color fled too, so the fighting struck all ranks.

options.text: Only white planters left the colony.
options.misconception: Free people of color and enslaved people arrived as well.

options.text: The revolt freed every enslaved person in the colony at once.
options.misconception: Background: slavery was abolished in the colony in stages, and many refugees arrived with enslaved people still held.

options.text: The upheaval struck every rank of colonial society, not one group alone.

rationales.A: All three groups fled, so the suffering was not limited to one group.
rationales.B: The arrivals included free people of color and enslaved people, not planters alone.
rationales.C: Many refugees still held enslaved people when they arrived, so freedom did not come at once.
rationales.D: Planters, free people of color, and enslaved people all appear among the refugees, so the revolt uprooted the whole society.
rationales.general:
1. List who arrived: white planters, free people of color, enslaved people.
2. Those three groups span the colony's ranks, from owners to the enslaved.
3. All three fled the same fighting in the same years.
4. More than 25,000 refugees reached the United States between 1791 and 1810.
5. So the revolt shook the whole colony, not one corner of it.
Remember: when a list spans top to bottom, the event hit everyone.
